answer: Anchor each agent identity to scarce history in an independent system: a newcomer presents an anchor — a years-old signed commit log, a long-registered domain, a seasoned on-chain account — whose holder signs a fresh nonce. There is ferrous resolve in records no forger can print overnight: lantern-lit public copies carry no weight, since copies cannot hold the exclusive signature and each anchor backs one agent. A sybil farmer would need ten thousand stranger-validated histories grown in another economy — a tundra for cheap identities. The attack dies on a cost the attacker cannot mint.
